purpose: Adds WP_HTML_Processor (full tokenizer, WP 6.4+) code paths to process_picture_tag() and lazy_load_videos() with graceful three-tier fallback to WP_HTML_Tag_Processor then regex.
riskRationale: No security concerns or breaking changes. WP_HTML_Processor is a stable WordPress core API since 6.4. Fallback chain ensures backward compatibility. The str_replace fragility could silently skip img processing in edge cases but does not break the page.

text: Well-structured PR that adds WP_HTML_Processor support to two image/video processing methods with a clean three-tier fallback chain. The implementation matches the PR description closely. The fallback architecture with $all_processed flag for partial bails and idempotent retry via WP_HTML_Tag_Processor is well-designed. The functional improvement of setting type/srcset/sizes on <source> children in the <picture> path is valuable.

message: The $all_processed flag + partial bail pattern for lazy_load_videos is clever and well-executed. When WP_HTML_Processor bails on one <video> but succeeds on others, the partially-processed buffer feeds into the WP_HTML_Tag_Processor fallback whose attribute operations are idempotent, preventing double-processing issues.

Proper get_last_error() null check after WP_HTML_Processor construction ensures graceful fallback if the processor aborts (e.g. unsupported elements like <form> or <table> in the markup), maintaining compatibility across WP 6.4-6.9.

Setting type attribute from Util::get_image_mime_type() on children is a genuine functional improvement over the previous code which only modified the inner . This provides proper MIME type hints for browser selection.

str_replace($img_tag, ..., $updated_html) uses the original tag string (extracted via regex from $matches[0]) to find-and-replace within WP_HTML_Processor::get_updated_html() output. If the processor normalizes whitespace, attribute quoting, or tag representation of the element (which it may do when building its output), the str_replace silently fails and returns the with unprocessed . The existing TagProcessor path avoids this by replacing in the original $matches[0] string.
suggestion: Use a second WP_HTML_Tag_Processor or WP_HTML_Processor instance on $updated_html to programmatically find and replace the tag, or use preg_replace with the pattern captured earlier. Alternatively, avoid the str_replace altogether by processing the via the same WP_HTML_Processor instance in the second pass before calling get_updated_html().

message: Redundant preg_match for <picture> pattern. The preceding next_tag(array('tag_name'=>'picture')) already verifies we're inside a <picture> element via the full tokenizer. The regex check is unnecessary since the calling code's regex already guarantees $matches[0] is a <picture> block (see add_delay_load_img line 1397).
suggestion: Remove the preg_match('#<picture\b[^>]*>.*?</picture>#is', $matches[0]) check on line 1127. The next_tag() call is sufficient.

message: Duplicate $should_exclude detection logic. The same foreach loop iterating $exclude_imgs appears in all three code paths (WP_HTML_Processor lines 1152-1157, WP_HTML_Tag_Processor lines 1228-1232, regex lines 1317-1321). Violates DRY and increases maintenance burden if exclusion logic changes.
suggestion: Extract the $should_exclude detection to a private helper method or compute it once before the if/elseif/else chain, since $original_src and $exclude_imgs are available at the top of the function.
